::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Matrix equation / Rewrite formula](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3110646/matrix-equation-rewrite-formula), asked by [DerCoder](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/644193/dercoder) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2019-02-12; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I´m looking for a solution for matrix **W**.
> Can anyone help me pls?
>
>
> $$\mathbf W \cdot A =\mathbf W + A$$
>
> $$A = 
> \left(
>     \begin{matrix}
>     2 & 1 \\
>     1 & 3 \\
>     \end{matrix}
> \right)$$
>
>
> My solution:
> **W** = $\left(\frac{A}{A-1}\right)$
> Is this correct? 
> Because $A-1$ is not possible - in my opinion (I thought you can´t subtract an integer from a matrix)
:::

You're close.  If $\mathbf{W}A = \mathbf{W} + A$, then
$$\mathbf{W}(A-I) = A$$
where $I$ is the $2\times2$ identity matrix.  Then
$$\mathbf{W} = A(A-I)^{-1}$$
if $A-I$ is invertible.  Can you take it from there?
